newsitem.title: CHINA: GUANGDONG BREWERY ENDS DEBUT SHARPLY UP.
newsitem.headline: GUANGDONG BREWERY ENDS DEBUT SHARPLY UP.

text.p: Shares of Guangdong Brewery Holdings Ltd, a unit of Guangdong Investment Ltd, bucked a mild pull-back in the market and ended their first day of trading sharply up from their issue price.
"It performed very well," said Raymond Jook, associate director of China research of SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"Strong Chinese parent backing and hopes of asset injections were the driving force behind the buying interests."
Guangdong Brewery shares, one of the most heavily traded stocks by turnover, ended at their day's high of HK$2.80 each, up HK$1.00 or 55.6 percent from their HK$1.80 issue price.
Volume was 167.82 million shares worth HK$398.68 million.
The shares moved in a range of HK$2.10 to HK$2.80.

"Its fundamentals are seen strong. The company is expected to continue buying other Chinese brewery plants and expanding its sales network, which can boost its asset base and outlook," said Hugo So, analyst at Yamaichi International.
"It is one of the very few aggressive brewers in China, and is proved by its sound track record," So said.
The brewer offered 350 million shares at HK$1.80 each, representing a proforma fully-diluted price to earnings multiple (P.E.) of 20.9 times.

In the issue, the 96.6 million shares offered for public subscription were 38.5 times oversubscribed. A further 218.4 million shares were offered to Guangdong Investment's existing shareholders and 35 million shares were offered to employees.
Guangdong Brewery is involved in production, distribution, and sales of "Kingway" beer. It has two production plants in Shenzhen and a sales network of about 200 distributors in China.

"Though the P.E. is a bit high, we still recommend a long term buy because we expect the company to achieve a stronger earnings growth in 1998 following an increase in production capacity to 400,000 tonnes from 200,000 tonnes," Jook said.
"Beer consumption is also seen to be increased in line with the economic growth in China and after the company successfully penetrates into markets outside Guangdong province," Jook said.
The brewer had said in its listing prospectus it planned to produce 400,000 tonnes of beer by early 1998.
It said it would use the net proceeds from the issue to upgrade and expand its brewery plants in Shenzhen and its sales network in China.
